title.narrative: Lifesaving emergency livelihoods assistance to cyclone affected most vulnerable farmers and fisher folks in Rakhine State, Myanmar.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspangtCyclone Mocha caused lives and devastation to the livelihoods of thousands of people in Rakhine State, Myanmar. About 279,147 hectares of cropland were flooded and substantial quantities of rice as well as vegetable seed stocks as well and other household assets have been damaged or lost. The fisheries sector, a main source of livelihood in Rakhine state, was also heavily impacted, with at least 50% of fishing equipment destroyed or damaged. The effects of the Cyclone will further impact the already severe food security situation in Rakhine, which is one of the most food-insecure states in Myanmar. As of late 2022, the FAO-WFP Food Security Monitoring Livelihood Survey reported that a significant number of people in Rakhine State (59% of respondents) were resorting to emergency or crisis-level measures to sustain their livelihoods. This was the highest percentage recorded among the fourteen assessed state/regions in the country. lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThelt/spangtltspangt project will target Cyclone Mocha most affected communities in Sittwe, Ponnagyun, and Rathedaung townships of Rakhine State, to support 35,000 people (7,000 households: HHs). Villages of the aforementioned townships will be prioritized based on the magnitude of the impact of the cyclone. FAO recently conducted key informant interviews in eleven townships of Rakhine state that will determine the extent of the damage and losses per township. The project will specifically target poor women, mothers with children under 5 years old, women-headed households, and other HH with high vulnerability and low resilience index.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project will restore and protect the livelihoods of the severely affected and vulnerable small-scale farmers, fisher folk, and landless seasonal / farm workers in Sittwe, Ponnagyun and Rathedaung townships in Rakhine state, impacted by Cyclone Mocha and compounding shocks. A total of 20,000 people (4,000 HH) will be provided with farm inputs for each to establish an average 0.25 acres of vegetable garden growing 6 kinds of vegetables for food consumption, with excess to be sold in the local market for income. A total of 7,500 people (1,500 HH) fisher folk affected by the cyclone whose fishing equipment was damaged will be supported with fishing gear/equipment in order to resume their livelihoods. In addition, a total of 7,500 people (1,500 HH) will be provided with temporary employment through cash-for-work (CfW) for 20 to 30 working days to repair/rehabilitate small irrigation and other community-based infrastructures.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtOne month after the cyclone the markets in project townships have resumed to about normal with the availability of basic commodities, except for construction materials, thus the use of cash transfer programming through CfW would be feasible. In all project interventions mentioned above, attention will be paid to the disproportionate compounded impact of the disaster and crisis on women and women-headed households in vulnerability ranking and selection of beneficiaries.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtltspangtFAO long-term local partner (LP) - People for People (PfP) – has worked with FAO for the past 3 years, will support community consultations, validation of and communication with beneficiaries, distribution of agriculture and fisheries inputs procured by FAO, cash for work, and awareness-raising activities. Another LP, Action Based Community Development (ABCD) will also be selected to work in the project townships, and be provided with technical inputs, supervision, and quality control by FAO. PfP will work in Ponnagyun, while ABCD will be implemented in Sittwe and Rathedaung. Post-distribution monitoring will be also conducted by the local partners and analyzed by FAO. PfP and the LP will ensure close coordination and maintain good working relationships with their respective village authorities, key stakeholders, and the community in general. The cash payout for the Cash for Work laborers will be paid by the local partner or by a financial service provider.lt/spangtlt/pgt
